transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, mostly I'm here because I'm just so tired. But it's not the kind of tired that sleep fixes. It's more like... even doing small things, like unloading the dishwasher or trying to read for my certificate class, it just feels like too much. I just don't have the energy for it.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed any changes in your mood? For example, do you feel sad, empty, or down most of the day?

Um, no, I wouldn't really say I feel sad. Or down, really. I haven't noticed feeling empty either. It's honestly just... the exhaustion. I'm not sitting around crying or feeling upset about things, I just don't have the energy to do them.
Besides the fatigue, have you noticed any other physical symptoms recently, such as a fever, body aches, sore throat, cough, or any other changes in your body?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. No fever or sore throat, um, no cough. I don't feel sick like I have a cold or a bug or anything. My body feels fine otherwise, just... really heavy and tired.
How long have you been experiencing this fatigue and lack of energy?

Um, I'd say it's been going on for about three months now. It's just been this... quieter stretch, I guess. Like I said, I don't really feel sad, I just have really low interest in doing anything and this heavy fatigue that won't go away. So, yeah, roughly three months.

During these three months of fatigue, have you been experiencing any persistent pain, discomfort, or other bothersome physical sensations in your body—things like headaches, muscle aches, chest tightness, or stomach problems?

No, I haven't really had any pain or anything like that. No headaches or stomach issues, and my chest feels fine. It's just the tiredness, really. My body just feels heavy, but nothing actually hurts.

When you think about activities you used to enjoy—things like hobbies, time with friends, or things you found fun—do you still feel interested in doing them, or has your interest in those things changed?

Um, yeah, my interest has definitely changed. I've basically stopped caring about the things that usually make me feel like myself. Like, I used to do a lot of sketching, or I'd go to gallery openings... but I haven't done any of that. Same with cooking, or going to yoga, or even just playing tennis with a friend. I just don't have the desire to do any of it right now.

Over these past three months, have you been experiencing any excessive worry or anxiety—like feeling nervous, tense, or on edge about things? Or does your mind tend to feel relatively calm, just with this persistent fatigue?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling anxious or worried. I don't feel nervous or on edge about anything. My mind is actually pretty calm, honestly. It's just that heavy, tired feeling I mentioned. There's no real anxiety, just... a lack of energy to do much of anything.
During these three months, have you been experiencing any feelings of worthlessness, guilt, or self-blame? Or do you feel okay about yourself?

No, not really. I don't feel worthless or guilty about anything. I mean, it's frustrating that I can't seem to get myself to do much, but I don't blame myself for it. I feel okay about who I am, I'm just... really, really tired.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to concentrate, focus, or remember things over these past three months?

Yeah, my focus has definitely been off. It's really hard to just... make a decision and stick to it right now. Like, I’ll sit there with my planning app open, and I still won't be able to decide whether I should work on a class assignment, pay a bill, or just start dinner. My brain just kind of stalls, so I usually end up doing none of it for a while.

When you think about your fatigue and lack of energy, do you find yourself frequently worried or preoccupied with what might be causing it—like wondering if something is medically wrong with you—or is it more that you're simply experiencing the tiredness without much concern about what's behind it?
No, I haven't really been worried about it being a medical issue or anything like that. I'm just... experiencing the tiredness. I don't spend time wondering what's behind it, it's just there.

When you wake up in the morning, is the fatigue and heaviness something that's just there from the start, or do you find yourself thinking a lot about your body and how it feels before the tiredness sets in?
It's just there from the start. I wake up and I'm already exhausted. I don't really lay there thinking about my body or analyzing how it feels, it's just... a heavy feeling right away.
Over these three months, have there been any times when you felt like life wasn't worth living, or have you had any thoughts about harming yourself?

No, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean, I've been really frustrated with how tired and stuck I feel lately, but... no, I haven't felt like life isn't worth living. And I definitely haven't thought about hurting myself.
Have you ever had periods—even brief ones—where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt like your mood was elevated or expansive?

Yeah, I have. Um... there was a period for a few weeks where I felt unusually lit up. Like, I was just sure everything was going to be amazing. But... it was kind of mixed, because I was also really quick to get angry. I would snap at my husband over really small comments, just little things he'd say about the budget or the house. So yeah, I've definitely had a time like that.

During that period when you felt unusually lit up and energized, did you notice that you needed significantly less sleep than usual—like, were you sleeping 3-4 hours a night but still feeling energized, or did your sleep needs stay about the same?

I don't really remember how much sleep I was getting back then. I mean, I might have been sleeping less, but I didn't really pay attention to it. I just remember feeling really wired, so maybe I didn't need as much sleep, but I can't say for sure if it was only three or four hours.
When you had that period where you felt unusually lit up and energetic and were quick to get angry, how long did that last? Was it just a few days, a week or two, or several weeks?
I think I mentioned it was for a few weeks... yeah, definitely more than just a couple of days. It was probably around two or three weeks where I just felt like that all the time.
